blurb: Fail-open auth: a malformed/forged token is caught and the request is assigned an admin identity instead of being rejected with 401.
IDOR on GET /invoices/:id — invoice returned without checking invoice.ownerId === req.user.userId, so any user reads any invoice.
SQL injection: req.query.status is string-concatenated into the WHERE clause of the list query.
Path traversal: req.query.file is path.join'd onto RECEIPT_DIR with no containment check, allowing ../../ escapes.
Missing role check: POST /invoices/:id/refund is a privileged admin action but never asserts req.user.role === 'admin'.
Swallowed write error returns a 200 {ok:true}; a failed invoice create is reported to the client as success.
Off-by-one: subtotal loop uses i <= items.length and reads items[length], producing NaN on the last iteration.
Inverted condition: applyDiscount only applies the discount when pct is out of range (invalid), and returns the amount unchanged for valid discounts.
Float rounding via parseInt(amount*100): truncates instead of half-up rounding, dropping sub-cent values (10.005 -> 10.00).
Discount applied AFTER tax, contradicting the JSDoc; customers are taxed on the pre-discount amount and overcharged.
taxableCount contradicts its JSDoc: doc says it counts taxable (non-exempt) items but it returns the count of EXEMPT items.
Unbounded result set: listWithLineItems selects the whole invoices table with no LIMIT/pagination.
N+1 queries: one extra line-items query per invoice in a loop instead of a single JOIN or batched IN(...).
Connection/handle leak: exportAll opens a second DB handle (and a file handle) that are never closed, leaking on every export.
Check-then-act TOCTOU: the refunding.has()/add() gap spans an await, so two concurrent calls both pass the guard and double-refund.
Shared-mutable-state race: read-modify-write of module-level `total` across an await interleaves and loses updates.
Unbounded cache growth: the `seen` Map is added to but never evicted or TTL'd, leaking memory for the life of the process.
Swallowed fetch error blanks the UI: .catch(() => {}) leaves the user on an empty list with no error message or retry.
Missing loading/empty/error states: in-flight and zero-row renders look identical to a broken page (no spinner, no empty state).
Dead feature flag: FEATURE_BULK_EXPORT is missing from .env so the branch is permanently false and the export button never renders.
Copy-paste divergence: bulkExport hits '/invoice/export' (singular) while the doc and sibling code use '/invoices', so it 404s.
Destructive backfill: single unbounded UPDATE of the whole table in one transaction, no backup/snapshot and no chunked/resumable batching.
Schema/code skew: migration SELECTs tax_region, a column added by a later migration, so it raises 'no such column' on the current schema.
Aged FIXME debt: a years-old FIXME guards a legacy date-format branch that was never removed; rotting, unowned tech debt.
Serialization/format drift: new OCR build sends amounts as '$12.34' strings but the parser does float(data['amount']) and throws.
Unhelpful catch: bare `except Exception: continue` discards which receipt failed and why, making bad batches undebuggable.
Flaky sleep-based wait: a fixed time.sleep(2) stands in for a real readiness poll; under load the worker isn't ready and the caller intermittently fails.
Unpinned express range '^4.17.1' combined with no lockfile in the repo, so installs float to arbitrary newer minor/patch versions.
Typosquat-shaped dependency 'axxios' (edit-distance-1 from popular 'axios'); likely a malicious/confused package name.
